page.overview:
What is The Pokémon Company?

The company was founded on April 23, 1998, as the Pokémon Center Company to manage the Pokémon Center retail stores in Japan. In 2000, it was reorganized and renamed The Pokémon Company to take over full responsibility for the Pokémon brand worldwide. It is a joint venture between Nintendo, Game Freak, and Creatures Inc..

The company originated as the Pokémon Center Company, Ltd. in April 1998, a business created by Nintendo, Game Freak, and Creatures to manage official Pokémon retail outlets known as Pokémon Centers in Japan. At the time, demand for licensed Pokémon products had surged globally, especially following the release of . Tsunekazu Ishihara, then of Creatures, who was overseeing licensing approval, found the scale of operations too large to manage efficiently under the original structure.

To streamline management and facilitate long-term growth of the brand—particularly with annual anime films and consistent global merchandising—a new entity was established. In October 2000, the company was renamed The Pokémon Company, assuming responsibility for the brand's comprehensive management.

Nintendo executive Satoru Iwata later stated that helping establish The Pokémon Company was one of his early projects upon joining Nintendo's board of directors.
